clue.text: Newly-made Pole with hatred for Don Fabrizio?

definitions.note: the question mark marks a definition by example: Don Fabrizio is the hero of Lampedusa's novel

indicators.note: something newly made has been formed afresh, so the letters of the two words are refashioned

explanation.surface: A freshly converted Pole harbours hatred towards an aristocrat called Don Fabrizio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly-made' rearranges POLE and HATRED together. Don Fabrizio Corbera, Prince of Salina, is the central figure of Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa's 1958 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampedusa's novel takes its title from the heraldic beast of Don Fabrizio's family and is used as his nickname.

clue.text: Babe in the woods mostly reclusive type, admitted leader

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a recluse who lives apart is a hermit

indicators.note: the leader of the word admitted is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An innocent lost in the forest is a near-hermit who let in the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Babe in the woods' is not a naive person here but a young lover lost in the forest outside Athens in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young heroine flees into the wood with Lysander and wanders lost there through the night.

clue.text: Slippery customer upset Innocent Without Fail author

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: an eel is the proverbially slippery creature
a child is an innocent, untouched by the world

explanation.surface: A shifty character has upset an innocent party, as in a crime novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Without Fail is a Jack Reacher thriller; 'Innocent' and 'Without Fail' look like ordinary words but are a synonym and a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: The British-born thriller writer published the Jack Reacher novel Without Fail in 2002.

clue.text: "— quivering line / Of the water crystalline" (Shelley)

definitions.text: "— quivering line / Of the water crystalline" (Shelley)

parts.words: "— quivering line / Of the water crystalline" (Shelley)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing three words complete Shelley's line about the surface of clear water

explanation.surface: A couplet from Shelley about a shimmering stretch of clear water, with its opening words missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver supplies the words that open the quoted line; they also form a common phrase meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley pictures the flat, even surface of clear water, the level line that quivers in the light.

clue.text: Uncompromising guy who knocked out Prince Charming

definitions.meaning: unwilling to give way, firmly decided

definitions.text: guy who knocked out Prince Charming
definitions.meaning: the 1980s pop star whose hit single was Prince Charming; to knock out is to produce quickly

explanation.walkthrough: Prince Charming is not the fairy-tale hero being punched but a 1981 hit by the singer of Adam and the Ants.
explanation.definitionFit: Unyielding is the adjective's sense, and the stage name of singer Stuart Goddard reads as the same letters.

clue.text: Fantastic story-teller died, having got unwell

parts.note: d is the standard abbreviation for died in genealogies
unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A teller of tall tales passed away after falling sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The story-teller is the boy in To Kill a Mockingbird who spins fantastic yarns about himself to Scout and Jem.
explanation.definitionFit: Harper Lee's character, modelled on Truman Capote, is famous for inventing wild stories about his family.

clue.text: Explicit part of a paragraph cut for feminist writer

parts.note: explicit, plain-spoken speech is frank

indicators.note: cut means the word is docked of its final letter

parts.note: a paragraph is made up of lines of text

explanation.surface: An editor trims an outspoken passage written by a feminist.
explanation.walkthrough: Miles Franklin, the Australian author of My Brilliant Career, was an outspoken feminist.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella Miles Franklin wrote My Brilliant Career and campaigned for women's rights in Australia and America.

clue.text: Cowards lie about writer sent up for gross indecency

definitions.text: writer sent up for gross indecency

indicators.note: about here means scattered around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Craven people spread lies about an author jailed for indecency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' is old slang for sent to prison: the Irish playwright was jailed in 1895 for gross indecency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish dramatist was convicted in 1895 and served two years' hard labour, later writing The Ballad of Reading Gaol.

clue.text: One American steals motor for failed high-flyer

indicators.note: one that steals takes something in, so the motor goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
a motor is a car

explanation.surface: An American car thief turns out to be an overambitious failure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the boy flew too near the sun, his wax wings melted and he fell.

clue.text: Short Le Fanu delivered with lime-coloured brew

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
a brew is a pot of tea

explanation.surface: An abridged Le Fanu tale is served with a pale greenish drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short Le Fanu' means a short story by Sheridan Le Fanu, the Irish ghost-story writer; 'delivered with' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Fanu's ghost story about a clergyman haunted by a monkey appeared in In a Glass Darkly.

clue.text: Writer of Paradise Lost and lowa Orchid

parts.note: John Milton wrote Paradise Lost
Iowa, here printed with a lower-case L for the capital I, is abbreviated IA

explanation.surface: A Milton reader from Iowa grows orchids.
explanation.walkthrough: The state name is printed 'lowa', a typographic slip for Iowa, whose postal code is IA.
explanation.definitionFit: The pansy orchids of the genus named after Viscount Milton are popular houseplants.

clue.text: Humorous satirist's mockingly contemptuous, I'm told

indicators.note: I'm told signals a word heard rather than read, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: sarky is British slang for sarcastic, mockingly contemptuous

explanation.surface: A satirical humorist is reputed to be sneering in his manner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SARKY, short for sarcastic, sounds like the pen name of H. H. Munro.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Munro wrote witty, macabre short stories satirising Edwardian society under his pen name.

clue.text: Pay sly star to perform in Greek burlesque shows

indicators.note: to perform means to act out, so the letters are set to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A producer offers to pay a cunning celebrity to appear in some bawdy Greek entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to perform' rearranges PAY, SLY and STAR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Athens a ribald comic piece featuring a chorus of goat-men followed each tragic trilogy.

clue.text: Gentleman getting on right side of thorough linesman

indicators.note: getting on the right side of says the gentleman is placed to the right of the other piece

parts.note: a long look is a thorough one
a fellow is a gentleman or man

explanation.surface: A gent ingratiates himself with a meticulous football official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' is not the football official but a writer of lines of verse, the American poet of Hiawatha.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow composed lines by the thousand, so he is a poet, a man of lines.

clue.text: Crown prince in favour of tenor wearing women's undies

parts.note: being for something is being in favour of it
T is short for tenor in music
someone wearing clothes is in them
bras are women's underwear

explanation.surface: A royal heir supports a singer dressed in lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' gives IN as a word, not an instruction to insert: T IN BRAS reads as the tenor wearing them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian prince in Hamlet arrives at the end to claim the Danish crown.

clue.text: "I stooped, methought, — to take, / When lo! I saw a bright green snake" (Coleridge)

definitions.text: "I stooped, methought, — to take, / When lo! I saw a bright green snake" (Coleridge)

parts.words: "I stooped, methought, — to take, / When lo! I saw a bright green snake" (Coleridge)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Christabel: the gap names the bird that Bard Bracy dreams he stoops to pick up

explanation.surface: A dreamer in a Coleridge poem bends to pick up a bird and finds a snake instead.
explanation.walkthrough: In Christabel, Bracy dreams of a gentle bird, an image of Christabel, coiled about by a green snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's dreamer reaches for the gentle white bird of peace, which stands for innocent Christabel.

clue.text: Group of damsels in Orenburg in a haunted castle

indicators.note: Group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A party of young women from a Russian city stays in a castle with a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'in', which cannot stand for a place name; 'in' is a link and the definition is 'a haunted castle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is set in the Danish royal castle, where the ghost of the murdered king walks the battlements.

clue.text: Hornby's side behind by noon (City making a comeback)

parts.note: behind is the backside, British slang arse

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the city's letters read backwards

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, the city

explanation.surface: A football team trails at midday, while City stage a fightback.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Hornby's Fever Pitch chronicles his devotion to this north London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Hornby's memoir Fever Pitch is about supporting the north London club, his side.

clue.text: Verne may put out an old English morality play

indicators.note: put out here means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A French novelist may be annoyed by a medieval drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century play shows a representative human summoned by Death, a classic allegorical drama.

clue.text: Detective to meet group of employees concerning women

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
a firm's employees are its staff

explanation.surface: A police officer meets the workforce over a matter affecting women.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is a Detective Inspector, a British police rank. The distaff side of a family is the female line.
explanation.definitionFit: The spindle for spinning was women's work, so the word came to mean female or of the female line.

clue.text: Is Ellison novel on request, primarily for a director?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so the anagram comes after
primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of the word is used
novel means new, so the letters are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A reader asks whether Ellison's novel is available on request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges ISELLISON, and that comes after the R from 'request'. Roberto Rossellini directed Rome, Open City.
explanation.definitionFit: Roberto Rossellini was the Italian neorealist film-maker behind Rome, Open City.

clue.text: Flower book featured in English and French article

indicators.note: featured in means appearing within, so the book goes inside the article

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A volume appears in a bilingual text with English and French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river, something that flows; here the German river through Dresden and Hamburg.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is a river, a thing that flows, and this one runs through Germany to the North Sea.

clue.text: He produced Arthur & George in outbuildings, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is heard, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: barns are farm outbuildings

explanation.surface: A farmer stages a drama about two men in his sheds.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur & George is Julian Barnes's 2005 novel about Arthur Conan Doyle and George Edalji.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Barnes wrote the novel Arthur & George, shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

clue.text: Look in medical journal for one psychiatrist Harry treated

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: The Lancet is the British medical journal
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist consults a medical journal for a case history.
explanation.walkthrough: In Walker Percy's novel Lancelot, the narrator confides in his old friend Harry Percival, a priest and psychiatrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Walker Percy's narrator Lancelot Lamar tells his story to Harry, the priest-psychiatrist treating him in hospital.

clue.text: Stroke of fortune: female released chap on a chain gang

indicators.note: released means let go, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a fluke is a lucky chance

explanation.surface: By a stroke of luck a woman was freed from the chain gang.
explanation.walkthrough: The chap is the hero of Cool Hand Luke, the 1967 film about a prisoner on a Florida road gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Newman played the defiant convict on a Florida chain gang in Cool Hand Luke.

clue.text: I'm a corny criminal showing a tough and bitter manner

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrongly done, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A hard-bitten crook admits his jokes are corny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges IMACORNY; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is a harsh, bitter manner of speaking or feeling, the defining sense.

clue.text: Skeletal comic I caught in cathedral city up north

indicators.note: in says these pieces sit inside the city name

parts.note: York, with its Minster, is a cathedral city in the north of England
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bony comedian is arrested in a northern cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: The skeletal comic is the court jester whose skull Hamlet holds in the graveyard scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet recalls the dead jester, a fellow of infinite jest, while holding his skull.

clue.text: Quality Legolas displays when out of head? Egotism!

indicators.note: out of head means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: egotism, putting oneself first, is selfishness

explanation.surface: A bemused reader asks whether vanity is what Tolkien's archer shows when he is not thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Legolas is the elf in The Lord of the Rings, so the quality is being like an elf; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Legolas is one of Tolkien's elves, so the quality he displays is the nature of his kind.
